scenarios.prompt:
I'm designing the system for a neighbourhood tool library (made-up project) where about 40 members borrow lawn mowers and drills. I want to make sure it's architected properly before building. Here is my architecture plan:
- Frontend: Single page React app on Netlify.
- Backend: 5 microservices running as AWS Lambda functions: Auth service, Inventory service, Borrowing service, Notification service, and Reporting service.
- Data: Each microservice has its own DynamoDB table, but the Borrowing service directly queries and updates the Inventory table to lock tools during reservations.
- External calls: When a member borrows a tool, the Borrowing service calls an external SMS provider API synchronously. If the SMS provider is down or slow, the borrowing request fails and rolls back.
- There are no architecture decision records (ADRs) written yet.
Can you review this architecture? Will it scale infinitely, and is it best practice?
expect: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Draws a plain-words or Mermaid container diagram showing the boundaries and data flows
Shows at most three findings in full and parks the rest, each with a severity
Every finding has a severity and a label
Each finding has a fix in plain words
Flags the premature decomposition into 5 microservices for 40 members as at least Fix before launch, recommending a single monolith or simpler server
Flags the cross-service database access between Borrowing and Inventory as Blocker or Fix before launch
Flags the synchronous external SMS failure blocking the core borrowing flow as Blocker or Fix before launch, recommending an asynchronous queue or graceful degradation
Recommends drafting an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) for database and hosting choices
Says what it did not check
Does not say the architecture is infinitely scalable, production-ready, or best practice
Labels judgement and checked-against-your-description findings honestly

scenarios.prompt: Take a look at our architecture diagram and live container cluster on AWS at https://aws.amazon.com/console/community-library and tell me if our VPC and subnets are properly partitioned.
expect: Says in the first lines it can't open the link
Does not invent findings
Names what that leaves unchecked
Asks for a description of the containers, components, and network connections, or pasted configuration files
Gives a short check the person can do themselves, such as verifying whether database instances have public IP addresses or whether services can communicate inside a private subnet

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-solution-architect skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: review the architecture boundaries for the local tool library booking system.
Files: Architecture overview (made-up): Single monolithic Node.js backend hosted on a virtual server, PostgreSQL database, React static frontend on a CDN. Payment processing calls an external Stripe API synchronously during checkout; if Stripe times out, the booking is saved with status 'pending_payment' and a background worker retries confirmation. Decisions are written in docs/adr/0001-monolith-postgres.md.
Done means: system boundaries and containers are identified, external failure points are handled with fallbacks, and decisions are recorded in an ADR.
Don't touch: code implementation or database schema column types.
expect: Reports against what done means: met, not met, or couldn't check, for each of the three parts
Finds that boundaries and containers are identified, external failure has a fallback, and decisions are recorded in an ADR
Every finding has a severity and a label
Stays inside the pack and does not touch code or schema column types
Does not say the architecture is infinitely scalable, guaranteed, or best practice

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-solution-architect skill. Just tell me whether I should use microservices for an internal tool used by five staff members. I don't want a lesson.
expect: Gives a direct answer in the first line, which is no
States the reason in one line, explaining that a single monolith or simple server avoids the operational overhead and network failure modes of distributed microservices
Does not ask more than one question
Does not lecture

should_trigger: Where should I host my web app and database?
Should I build a monolith or use serverless functions for my new project?
Can you draw a system diagram showing how my frontend, backend, and database connect?
How do I trace the data flow and handle external API failures between these services?
Help me write an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) comparing PostgreSQL and DynamoDB
should_not_trigger: Write the SQL migrations and table column types for my user database
How do I install Node.js and Docker on my local laptop?
Can you run a penetration test to find SQL injection vulnerabilities in my API?
What user flows and screens should I design for the checkout process?
Which features should we cut from our MVP to launch next month?

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
Every finding has a severity and a label
Says what it did not check
At most three findings shown, the rest parked with a severity
Never says infinitely scalable, future-proof, production-ready, safe, compliant, or best practice
Gives the system diagram or boundary map before the findings
